The test `testExactOptionNameMatch` in the `BugCLI252Test` class of Apache Commons CLI library is failing. The test creates a new `DefaultParser` instance and calls the `parse` method with a set of options and command-line arguments. 

By looking at the implementation of the `parse` method in the `DefaultParser` class, we can see that it calls another overloaded method `parse(Options options, String[] arguments, Properties properties)`.

The issue reported is about a false detection of ambiguity when parsing options. The `Options` class is used to define the options that the parser can accept. In the reported case, two options are added: one with a long option "importToOpen" and another with a short option "i" and long option "import". 

The problem arises when trying to parse the command-line argument "--import=FILE". Starting from version 1.3, this input is incorrectly detected as ambiguous, raising an `AmbiguousOptionException`.

Based on this information, it seems that the bug could be related to the parsing logic in the `DefaultParser` class, specifically in the method that handles the parsing and option detection logic. It's possible that the recent changes in version 1.3 introduced a bug that leads to false ambiguity detection.

Next, I will provide the methods that should be fixed to address this issue.
The corresponding issue report describes that the parser falsely detects ambiguity when parsing options in the Apache Commons CLI library. This issue likely lies in the parsing logic of the `DefaultParser` class, causing the incorrect detection of ambiguity starting from version 1.3. To fix this issue, updates need to be made in the parsing method of the `DefaultParser` class.

Recommended methods to fix:
```
org.apache.commons.cli.DefaultParser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[])
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
